headline: Leaked Omnicorp Employee Handbook Contains 'Impossible' Safety Guidelines
subheadline: Document instructs workers on 'temporal displacement protocol' and 'what to do if you encounter yourself'
summary: A purported Omnicorp Holdings employee handbook has surfaced online, containing safety protocols for scenarios that should not be physically possible.
content:
An anonymous source has leaked what appears to be an internal Omnicorp Holdings employee handbook to Threadit. The 847-page document contains standard corporate policies alongside instructions for situations that defy conventional understanding.

The handbook, titled "Omnicorp Holdings Associate Guidelines: Continuity Edition," includes expected sections on benefits, conduct, and workplace safety. But starting on page 47, the document takes an unusual turn.

**Section 4.7: Temporal Displacement Protocol**

"If you find yourself in a location or time period inconsistent with your scheduled shift, remain calm. Do not attempt to contact your past or future self. Do not interact with historical figures. Proceed to the nearest Continuity Station (marked with blue triangles) and await retrieval. Standard displacement events resolve within 8-47 minutes."

**Section 8.4: Encountering Yourself**

"In the event you encounter another version of yourself, do not make eye contact. Do not share information about future events. If physical contact occurs accidentally, report to HR immediately. The company is not liable for paradox-related injuries."

**Section 13: [REDACTED]**

The entire 13th section of the handbook is blank except for the header and a single instruction: "If you are reading this section, you are in the wrong timeline. Please report to Floor 13 for recalibration."

Omnicorp Holdings has not confirmed or denied the document's authenticity. A spokesperson stated: "Omnicorp Holdings has many internal documents covering many contingencies. We prepare our associates for all possibilities. This is standard corporate practice."

Labor attorney Sarah Mendez reviewed the handbook at reporters' request. "I've never seen anything like this," she said. "Some of these clauses aren't even legally enforceable because they describe events that can't happen. You can't waive liability for 'paradox injuries.' That's not a thing."

The handbook's benefits section, notably, appears generous: unlimited paid time off, comprehensive health coverage including "non-linear medical events," and a pension plan that "matures across all applicable timelines."

Employee reviews of Omnicorp on LinkedUp are sparse but consistently cryptic. One review, posted eight months ago, reads: "Great benefits. The work is meaningful. Hard to describe to family. Don't ask about the basement. 4.7 stars."

Dr. Elena Martinez was shown the leaked handbook. She read it silently for 47 minutes, then returned it without comment. When pressed, she said only: "I need to reconsider some assumptions I've made about this city."

The original Threadit post containing the handbook has been viewed 847,000 times. The anonymous poster has not been active since uploading the document. Their account name: "FormerAssociate_Timeline_C".
author: Diane Cheng, Investigative Reporter
